count_gate.note: printed difficulty table 6/6/4=16 AGREES with per-question tags; flagged counts answer-level flags; all carry the structural marks flag (addendum §4.5).

method_notes: Offset -11 (pdf 20 = folio 9; pdf 86 = folio 75). Q: q1-7 pdf20, q8-16 pdf21. A: keys 1-13 pdf86, 14-16 pdf87. KEY monotonic 1-16, no shift/insert/map.
Sections: I MCQ q1-4; II one word/sentence q5-9 (vsa); III two/three q10-13 (sa); IV five/six q14-15 (la); V seven/eight q16 (la).

MCQ: q1 key 'D) Darshanas (Philosophical Systems)' -> option D 'Philosophies' (letter D governs; key text is a gloss, benign flag); q2 key 'D) Has been practiced since ancient times.' = option D (minor case). q3/q4 clean. NOTE possible printed-key factual doubt q1 (foundations of Sanatana Dharma: key=Philosophies/D, option C=Vedas) -> review.
VSA q5-9 answer.value = sentence, no steps (3d); q8 key is a quoted mantra line.

Descriptive all SUB (heading 'X:' non-step): q10 4 steps, q11 4, q12 6, q13 1 (three branches printed comma-separated on one line -> one step per printed line), q15 5, q16 8 (title heading + lead 'It teaches that:' as step + 5 May-lines + 2 closing).

q14 KEY IS A 2-COLUMN TABLE (Vedic vs Present-Day). Ruled-table extraction (v2 §7 / §13.3): one step per printed row incl. header -> 7 steps (header 'Vedic Society | Present-Day Society' + 6 rows, cells joined ' | '); title is the non-step heading.
De-glue: q16 stem 'SanatanaDharma'->'Sanatana Dharma'. MARKS none printed -> all null/unassigned + structural flag (§4.5).

answer.value:
Differences Between Vedic Society and Present-Day Society
Vedic Society | Present-Day Society
Joint family system | Nuclear family system
Varna system | Caste system
Sanskrit language | Use of various languages
Animal husbandry and agriculture | Agriculture, industry, commerce, and other occupations
Vedic literature | Regional languages and literature
Property rights were communal | Property rights are mostly private

answer.value:
Note on the Shanti Mantra Found in the Vedas Related to Sanatana Dharma
The Shanti Mantra of the Vedas conveys a universal message of peace, harmony, and welfare. It teaches that:
May all people be happy.
May all be free from disease and worries.
May everyone experience goodness and auspiciousness.
May no one suffer from sorrow or misery.
May all living beings in the universe enjoy happiness, peace, and prosperity.
It emphasizes universal brotherhood and compassion.
It promotes the welfare of all creation without discrimination.
